page: Hetzner Cloud cax41 is an Arm-based cloud instance powered by Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.0 GHz. The virtual machine provides 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with single-threading, alongside 31.0 GB of system memory, which yields an approximate 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 1.95 GB per core. Local storage is provided through a bundled 320 GB NVMe SSD under a QEMU hypervisor architecture, while hardware acceleration via GPUs is omitted.

Benchmark evaluations reveal modest single-thread metrics alongside consistent multi-threaded throughput. The instance recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 1052.0 and a multi-core score of 8500.0, reflecting lower per-core frequency common to dense Arm deployments. However, parallel execution tests such as stress-ng multi-core reached 29117.84, Clang compilation scored 15304.0, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 61.84 GB/sec, demonstrating stable scaling across all 16 cores.

Memory bandwidth measurements reach 102.2 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 57.91 GB/sec for writes. The instance supports substantial transactional density, achieving 22.71 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 16.72 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Natural language model inference remains constrained by single-thread latency, producing 10.47 tokens per second on medium 7B models.

Positioned within Hetzner's cost-optimized tier, the cax41 provides an economical compute density profile utilizing shared host threads and integrated NVMe capacity. Because single-core execution and cryptographic speeds are comparatively subdued, the instance is less suited for latency-critical single-threaded software, but it represents an efficient platform for multi-threaded container deployments, web clusters, microservices, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Hetzner Cloud cax41 is a compute-oriented virtual server featuring 16 shared vCPUs on an Arm64 Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 31.0 GB of RAM and 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The configuration yields approximately 1.95 GB of memory per core without GPU capabilities. Benchmark data highlights typical Arm64 performance characteristics: single-core throughput is modest, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1052.0, whereas multi-core scalability remains solid, logging 8500.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 29117.84 in stress-ng. The instance also delivers 22.71 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 16.72 GB/sec of static web throughput. Operating under a shared-core resource profile, the cax41 offers strong resource density for parallel tasks, making it well matched for build farms, containerized microservices, distributed web serving, and general multi-threaded applications.
